spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation
 of the Twelve
 Judges

---


**
¶2.
** Twelve principles
 of divine discrimination
 exist
 —
 great
 and powerful
 ord
erings
 by
 which all interior
 states are
 tried
 and distinguished
. They
 proceed
 forth
 from the Divine
 Itself into
 the created
 mind. Each
 is
 appointed
 to its distinct
 work of
 separation
 according
 to the governing
 purpose
 that
 the
 Divine
 Good
 —
 which
 is the origin
 of
 all judgment
 and
 all
 order
 — has ent
rusted to them
. For
 He
, the supreme
 principle
 of all
 discrimination, who
 transc
ends every
 particular
 act
 of separation
, who ab
ides and
 is established in the infinite
 states
 of the Divine
 Itself —
 He is the Divine
 Good
,
 the Father, the
 origin of all that
 is.


---


**¶3.** The
 first
 principle
 of
 discrimination
 is the most
 interior celestial will —
 the earliest and in
most state of the human mind —
 which
 in
 the
 beginning subd
ued the ruling
 love
 of self
 that
 had seized
 domin
ion over what belongs to the Divine alone
. It
 rendered
 true
 judgment upon self
-love, because
 self
-love had ex
alted itself against a domin
ion that
 was never
 its own.

---

**
¶4.** The second principle of
 discrimination is the viv
ifying divine truth that
 proceeds from the Divine Good. It descended
 and raised
 up
 the celestial will when
 it had been overwhel
med.
 It also
 rendered
 judgment
 upon all
 the persu
asions of fals
ity from
 evil,
 which
 had corrupted and
 torn
 the
 external truths that clothe the most
 interior will.

---

**
¶5.** The third principle of
 discrimination is the divine sphere of celest
ial-
spiritual life — the great
 proce
eding of life
 from which all perception is
 born
. She
 ordered
 and
 established
 the interior regions of the mind according
 to the
 Divine
 pleasure
. She judged the dominant
 falsities in the higher
 understanding;
 she bound
 them
 and confined them firmly
 in the
 degree
 that is
 fitting for them.

---

**
¶6.** The fourth principle
 of discrimination is the divine ordering power
 that constructs the new state of b
lessedness in the
 regenerate mind. It jud
ged, according to the order
 of divine
 truth, the accumulated
 reserves
 of evil and falsity stored
 in the memory,
 so
 that spiritual
 death —
 separation
 from the Divine — may not rise
 up
 again from
 that
 time forward. It has constructed a firm
 contain
ment for hered
itary evil. And
 upon the highest
 degree
 of the regener
ate mind it has established
 the
 ruling
 authority of the
 celestial will
 and of
 all the
 prior
 states of divine truth that w
aged
 the
 struggle
 against the
 evil of
 self
-love and
 prev
ailed.

---

**¶
7.** The fifth principle of discrimination
 is divine
 truth in its sovereign
 authority,
 dwelling
 and
 established in the in
most expanse of the internal mind.
 It is the power
 that gov
erns all the expans
es of the mind from in
most to outmost,
 rendering
 true discrimination
 according
 to divine
 order
 upon
 all persu
asions and
 all
 ruling
 states
 in
 every
 degree of
 the understanding
.

---

**¶8
.** The sixth principle of discrimination is
 the third proceeding of divine truth into
 the lower degrees
 of the mind — that
 which descended
 and made
 the
 form of divine truth visible and perceiv
able. It purified wisdom
 from what had been commingled with
 falsity, separ
ating what
 was of
 its
 own nature from
 what belonged
 to the advers
ary.

---

**¶
9.** The
 seventh principle of discrimination 
*(
the
 text
 here
 is largely
 lost
)* operates
 among
 the states
 of the
 mind
 in their
 full
ness. It gives
 confirmation
 and
 victory to those states
 that
 are
 steadfast in
 truth, but
 it
 condemns those states
 that are confirmed
 in falsity. For
 those
 who pers
evere,
 it becomes
 the successive
 degrees of progression through truth toward good;
 but
 those
 confirmed
 in evil it
 c
asts down
 into
 the lowest
 states
 of falsity —
 the hells.

---

**
¶10.** The eighth principle
 of discrimination is the
 Divine
 Wisdom
 Itself in
 its fullness —
 the
 source from
 which all truths of doctrine proceed.
 For
 after
 the form
 of divine truth had been made manifest and
 wisdom
 had begun
 to be
 separated from falsity, a
 great
 uprising
 of
 falsities
 from evil was stirred in
 every degree of the mind,
 above
 and below. Then the
 Divine Wisdom Itself was
 sent forth
.
 It descended
 and rendered
 judgment throughout
 all
 the expans
es of the understanding
. It separated those
 states
 confirmed
 in truth from those states
 confirmed in falsity.

---


**¶11.** The ninth
 principle of discrimination is the pure affection
 of truth
 — the love of truth for its
 own sake —
 which capt
ivated the desires
 of the
 evil
 aff
ections by
 the beauty of its
 own form
, drawing out
 and
 gathering
 to
 itself whatever
 in
 them
 belonged
 to the Divine
. It renders
 judgment
 upon the fals
ity
 that corru
pts living
 truth and upon
 the falsity that exists where truth is
 altogether
 absent.


---

**¶12.
** The tenth principle of discrimination is the
 disc
erning power
 that
 dw
ells in the rational
 mind, which stands between the spiritual and
 the
 natural degrees and
 judges
 all the
 states of the natural man
. It makes
 a separation between what
 is good and what is evil, setting
 apart what
 has
 been reformed
 from what remains
 in disorder
.

---

**¶13
.** The eleventh principle of discrimination
 is the divine
 truth that
 illuminates the understanding from within,
 which
 comes
 and
 becomes
 present in the natural mind. It cho
oses and
 calls
 forth
 the internal
 church within the person;
 it removes
 the cov
erings of appearances and
 separates wisdom
 from falsity,
 setting genuine
 truth apart from the disorder of the unre
generate will.

---

**
¶14.** The twelf
th principle of discrimination is the divine
 providence
 operating
 through the inmost conscience —
 which
 is at
 once the call of divine truth and the
 willing response of the regenerate will —
 and which
 is established in the fundamental constituent
 states of the natural mind. It is
 the principle
 that makes the
 final
 separation
 between good
 and evil.
 And
 at
 the last
 it
 g
athers together
 all
 that has been recovered and
 forms
 it
 into the ultimate embod
iment of the regenerate person —
 the completed
 human
 form
 of
 all
 rec
laimed wisdom.
 And
 it separates wisdom
 from falsity for
 the final
 time.

---

**¶
15.** These are the twelve great
 and powerful principles
 of divine discrimination that were sent forth.
 They proceeded
 from the one
 supreme
 origin
 of all judgment,
 which transc
ends every
 particular act of separation.
 He
 is the Divine Good that
 is
 hidden
 and immeasurable, the One
 who is
,
 who ab
ides in
 the infinite states of the Divine Itself
 upon
 the supreme
 authority
 of divine
 truth — which
 is the sovereign
 power
 of divine order
 established
 etern
ally in His
 own
 kingdom.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Twelve judges exist; the great mighty givers of judgement! They were sent and came from the exalted greatness to this place. They were assigned to different works according to the command that the Judge, who belongs to the greatness, entrusted to all these judges. Now he, the great Judge, he who transcends all the judges, who exists and is established in the aeons of greatness; he is the Father of Greatness.

The first judge is the First Man, he who humiliated the ruler of Darkness in the beginning. He judged him according to a judgement of righteousness; for he had exalted himself against a kingdom that was not his own.
The second judge is the Living Spirit, he who came and bore up the Man. He too made a judgement on all the powers of darkness; which had wounded the garments of the First Man.

The third judge is the Mother of Life, the Great Spirit, she who beautified and set up the heavenly part of the universe, according to her pleasure; which [was entrusted to] her. She judged the rulers above; she fettered and set them firmly in the place that is fitting for them.

The fourth judge is the Great Builder, he who built the new aeon of joy. He judged, according to a judgement of righteousness, the storehouses of the enemy; that death may not well up from this time on. He has constructed a prison for the enemy. Also, upon the crown of the building he has constructed a throne for the First Man and all the fathers of light; they who engaged the struggle with the evil one and were victorious over him.

The fifth judge is the great King of Honour, he who dwells and is established in the seventh firmament. He is the judge of all the firmaments who gives a true judgement, according to a judgement of righteousness, upon all the powers and all the kingdoms of the firmaments.

The seventh judge is [the Column of Glory, the Perfect Man,] [he who is established among] the worlds [and gives judgement therein. He gives the victory to] they who are steadfast; but he condemns the ones who are convicted [in their wickedness.] [For the steadfast,] he shall become for them the steps of the way (?) [to the heights]; but the convicted he sweeps and casts out to the depths.

The eighth judge is Jesus the Splendour, the father of all the apostles; because after the Ambassador had displayed his image and the light was taken [upward from them,] a mass of rulers rose up from above and below. Then they sent Jesus the Splendour. He came [from the heights;] [and] he descended and made a judgement in the firmaments. He separated the steadfast from the convicted.

The ninth judge is the Virgin of Light, [she who seized the heart] of the powers by her image, gathering her own ones into her. She makes a judgement on the ruler of the moist, and the ruler of the dry.
The tenth judge is the Judge who dwells in the atmosphere, judging all mankind. He makes a separation between they who are good and they who are evil, setting apart the righteous from the sinners.

The eleventh judge is the Light Mind, he who shall come and appear in the world. And he chooses the holy church, and he unveils [the hidden things] and separates light from darkness, and sets the truth apart from lawlessness.

The twelfth judge is the great counsel, which is the summons and the obedience, which is appointed in the elements. It is the one that makes a separation between the good and the evil ones. At the end also it can gather itself together and sculpt its own self in the Last Statue. And it separates light from darkness.

These are the twelve great and mighty judges who were sent. They came from the great Judge, he who transcends all the judges. He is the Father that is hidden and immeasurable, the one who exists; who is established in the aeons of greatness upon the great throne of honour, which is the King of Honour [established for ever] in his kingdom.

The sixth judge is [
the Th]ird Ambassador,
 he who came and displayed his image.
 He purified the light [from the
 darkness with] which his own [was
 commingled; and] also of
 the enemy, he has [rendered judg
ement.]
